feature_results.rationale: Documented project/user hooks.json configuration launches custom scripts before and after agent lifecycle stages, including generic tool use, shell execution, reads, edits, and subagent spawning. Hooks can block or modify actions, not merely notify an external service.

evidence.excerpt: They run before or after defined stages of the agent loop and can observe, block, or modify behavior.
Exit code `2` - Block the action (equivalent to returning `permission: "deny"`)

constraints.description: Cloud agents support command-based repository hooks but not prompt-based hooks or local user hooks. Hooks do not run during early read-only exploratory cloud turns; some IDE/session/MCP-specific events are unavailable in cloud agents.
Dashboard-distributed team and enterprise-managed hooks for cloud agents require Enterprise; project hooks are separately supported.
Permission hooks reject invalid JSON/schema output, and exit code 2 blocks the action, but other hook failure exit codes proceed by default (fail-open).

queries: Find official Cursor documentation URLs for agent hooks, custom subagents and their tool restrictions, native non-MCP custom tool registration, permissions, and Plan Mode. Search only cursor.com/docs and cursor.com/changelog; identify original pages, not forum posts.

feature_results.rationale: Local agent terminal sandboxing has configurable outbound network policy, not merely process isolation. sandbox.json supports default allow/deny, domain and CIDR allowlists, and overriding deny rules; users can select allowlist-only networking and enterprise admins can enforce team networking rules. This finding does not assert that the same configuration governs Cloud Agents or every agent tool.

evidence.excerpt: Network traffic is denied by default. Only the listed domains are reachable.
The `allow` and `deny` arrays accept three pattern formats:

Admins can override which modes are available for their users, configure the sandbox networking rules for terminal commands, set a [team read policy](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes.md#team-read-policy), and more.

constraints.description: Confirmed for sandboxed local terminal commands. Run Modes documentation describes macOS Seatbelt (Cursor v2.0+) and Linux Landlock/seccomp with kernel 6.2+, Landlock v3, and unprivileged user namespaces; unsuitable Linux environments fall back to approval. No Windows sandbox support is asserted.

The default network mode combines sandbox.json with Cursor's built-in package/tool domains. Select sandbox.json Only for a custom allowlist without those defaults. Allow All permits unrestricted sandbox networking; actions outside the sandbox are not covered by its egress rules. Cloud Agents do not use local Run Modes.
Network deny rules take priority; team-admin policy and hardcoded protections cannot be weakened by local files. Private address and metadata endpoints are blocked by default.

queries: Find official Cursor documentation for agent sandbox network allowlist firewall controls, enterprise audit logs SAML roles, data residency, DPA, encryption at rest, and IP indemnification public code filter. Search only cursor.com and docs.cursor.com; provide original official URLs. (no relevant results)

feature_results.rationale: An Agent checkpoint captures all modified files and a single restore reverts all files to that checkpoint, rather than requiring file-by-file or hunk-by-hunk undo. This is session-wide code rollback, not a rollback of conversation history, command side effects, or the whole operating environment.

evidence.excerpt: Checkpoints save snapshots of your codebase during an Agent session. Agent automatically creates them before making significant changes, capturing the state of all modified files.
If Agent takes a wrong turn, click any checkpoint in the chat timeline to preview your files at that point, then restore to revert all files to that state.

constraints.description: Restoring reverts files only and does not remove conversation messages. Checkpoints are stored locally, separate from Git, and intended to undo Agent changes.

queries: Find official Cursor documentation for Agent checkpoints restore all changes, parallel independent agents, terminal execution approvals, and automatically iterating on failing tests. Prefer cursor.com/docs pages; provide original page URLs.

feature_results.rationale: Enterprise customers receive per-event audit logs for authentication, membership, roles, API keys, settings and integrations, exposed through the Admin API. Teams and Enterprise also have administrator-visible usage dashboards and CSV downloads. The supplied partial criterion applies because per-event audit logging and analytics API access are restricted to Enterprise, rather than being generally available across team plans.

evidence.excerpt: Audit logs record who changed what in your team and organization: sign-ins, membership, roles, API keys, settings, integrations, Cloud Agent environments, Grok Bot configuration, and Origin repositories.
The Admin API returns one flat object per event:
Usage Analytics are available for Team and Enterprise customers.
Team admins have access to data for themselves and all other users in the team.

constraints.description: Audit logs are available on Enterprise. Teams receive analytics dashboards; programmatic analytics access is Enterprise-only.
Audit payloads exclude prompts, agent outputs, generated code and credentials. Failed sign-ins and Cloud Agent automation runs are not logged by this channel.
Usage Analytics collects data only from clients version 1.5 or higher.

feature_results.rationale: Bugbot is a dedicated hosting-platform PR review workflow, not an ad hoc chat request. It analyzes PR diffs, posts explanations and suggested fixes, and automatically reruns on PR updates. The accepted GitHub integration source independently documents connecting repositories for Bugbot.

evidence.excerpt: Bugbot analyzes PR diffs and leaves comments with explanations and fix suggestions. It runs automatically on each PR update or manually when triggered.
The Cursor GitHub app connects your repositories so you can use features like [Cloud Agents](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent.md) and [Bugbot](https://cursor.com/docs/bugbot.md).

constraints.description: Connect a supported source-control provider and enable Bugbot on the selected repositories. Documentation lists Origin, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps.
Individual repository settings restrict Bugbot to PRs authored by the user; enabled team repositories can be reviewed for all contributors.
Bitbucket Cloud and Azure DevOps Services support are listed as public beta.
Bitbucket Data Center support is listed for Teams and Enterprise.
Bitbucket Data Center supports automatic reviews only, without manual review triggers or Autofix.

feature_results.rationale: Cursor documents plain-language-driven refactoring through Agent, which locates relevant files and edits multiple files. The prompting reference explicitly describes multi-file refactoring, going beyond single-symbol rename or manual IDE commands. This establishes the capability, not a guarantee of behavioral equivalence; tests and human review remain necessary.

evidence.excerpt: Agent can build features from scratch, refactor existing code, fix bugs, write tests, and run shell commands. Give it a task in plain language and it figures out which files to read, what changes to make, and how to verify the result.
**More capable models** are better for complex reasoning and multi-file refactoring

constraints.description: Cursor recommends more capable models for complex reasoning and multi-file refactoring; model selection affects task suitability.
Agent edits workspace files without approval and saves changes immediately; use version control and verification rather than assuming a pre-apply gate.

feature_results.rationale: Cursor explicitly documents generating unit tests for an existing named service file, matching the repository's test patterns, and generating integration and end-to-end tests across multiple frameworks. This is documented test generation, rather than an incidental example of general code generation.

evidence.excerpt: Cursor reads your code and generates tests that match your existing patterns.
Write unit tests for \{\{file:src/services/PaymentProcessor.ts}}. Cover the happy path and common error cases like invalid card numbers, expired cards, and insufficient funds.
Beyond unit tests, Cursor generates integration and end-to-end tests across frameworks: Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, pytest, Jest, and others.

constraints.description: Automatic execution and iteration on generated tests require enabling Auto-run. Test generation itself can be requested independently.

queries: GET https://cursor.com/product -> incidental test example insufficient for this criterion
SEARCH site:cursor.com tests lint read_lints official documentation
GET https://cursor.com/for/javascript-typescript -> confirms linting, not test generation
SEARCH site:cursor.com write tests unit generate unit or integration tests for function
GET https://cursor.com/for/test-generation -> confirmed original official text

feature_results.rationale: Agent independently completes complex coding tasks through repeated search, editing and terminal tool calls. Cloud Agents auto-run terminal commands to iterate on tests without step-by-step approval; local Run Modes also support reduced or no per-call confirmation. The capability is not limited to a fixed predefined workflow.

evidence.excerpt: Agent is Cursor's assistant that can complete complex coding tasks independently, run terminal commands, and edit code.
There is no limit on the number of tool calls Agent can make during a task.
Cloud Agents auto-run terminal commands so they can iterate on tests without stopping for approval on every step.

constraints.description: Local terminal commands require approval by default; Run Modes configure automatic execution. Cloud Agents auto-run commands, but open draft PRs for human review before merging.
Cloud Agents require a paid Cursor plan and are charged at API pricing for the selected model.

feature_results.rationale: Cloud Agents run independently of the user's connected local machine, and the Agents Window supports handing work to the cloud to keep working on its own. Completion notifications are explicitly documented for Slack. Extended-duration agents are separately subject to team controls.

evidence.excerpt: You can run as many agents as you want in parallel, and they do not require your local machine to be connected to the internet.
quickly move an agent from cloud to local to iterate quickly, and move it back to the cloud so it keeps working on its own.
When Cloud Agent completes, you get a notification in Slack and an option to view the created PR in GitHub.

constraints.description: Cloud Agents require a paid Cursor plan and model-based usage billing.
The cited completion notification path requires installing and configuring the Cursor Slack integration.
Team admins can enable or restrict extended-duration agents. Long-running is not yet available for multi-repo environments.

feature_results.rationale: Original official research pages explicitly describe natural-language semantic retrieval using a trained embedding model and codebase indexing. However, the current Search documentation describes exact-match/regex Instant Grep and states that Cursor does not store codebase embeddings for search. Its Explore subagent is a context-management mechanism, not evidence of relevance-ranked semantic retrieval. Scope and current-capability policy favor the documentation over research articles, but the fetched pages do not establish whether semantic retrieval survives in another supported product surface or whether the research claims are historical. A broader changelog search did not provide original verified deprecation/version evidence. Consequently neither a current has/partial claim nor a completed negative finding is warranted.

queries: GET https://cursor.com/docs/agent/tools/search -> Instant Grep and no stored embeddings
GET https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview -> search tools described without semantic retrieval
SEARCH Cursor official documentation semantic codebase search embeddings indexing versus Instant Grep removal semantic search. site:cursor.com
GET https://cursor.com/blog/semsearch -> original affirmative semantic-search text
GET https://cursor.com/data-use -> fetched text did not resolve search capability
GET https://cursor.com/docs/release-notes -> first 15000 characters of recent release timeline
SEARCH Cursor 3.12 changelog removal of semantic search or codebase embeddings site:cursor.com/changelog
access_gaps: The recent release-notes timeline was only partially read; no original official deprecation entry, effective version, or scope reconciliation was verified.
Current documentation versus semantic-search research articles remains insufficiently reconciled across product surfaces.

conflict.reason: Official research articles affirm semantic retrieval, whereas current technical documentation describes literal/regex search and no stored codebase embeddings. Current documentation has higher policy priority, but does not explicitly settle the availability of semantic retrieval across all supported surfaces.

conflicting_evidence.excerpt: One tool Cursor’s agent uses is semantic search, which retrieves segments of code matching natural language queries, such as “where do we handle authentication?”, in addition to the regex-based searching provided by a tool like grep.
Cursor does not upload file paths or code to build a search index, and it does not store embeddings of your codebase for search.

feature_results.rationale: Users can author named Markdown/YAML subagent definitions with their own prompt, description, model, and independently restricted write permissions via readonly. The documented read-only scope prohibits edits and state-changing shell commands, meeting the tool-scope requirement, although arbitrary per-role tool allowlists and separate MCP attachments are not documented in this file format. These are user-authored roles, not only the built-in Explore and Browser agents.

evidence.excerpt: You can also create subagents manually by adding markdown files to `.cursor/agents/` (project) or `~/.cursor/agents/` (user).
If `true`, the subagent runs with restricted write permissions (no file edits, no state-changing shell commands).

constraints.description: Documented file configuration offers readonly permission scoping, not a listed arbitrary tools field. Ordinary subagents inherit parent tools including MCP; cloud subagents instead use team-configured cloud MCP servers.
Configured models can fall back when blocked by an admin, unavailable on the plan, or requiring disabled Max Mode on a legacy request-based plan.
Subagents are documented for the editor, CLI, and Cloud Agents. Project definitions take precedence over user definitions with the same name.

queries: Find official Cursor documentation URLs for agent hooks, custom subagents and their tool restrictions, native non-MCP custom tool registration, permissions, and Plan Mode. Search only cursor.com/docs and cursor.com/changelog; identify original pages, not forum posts.
FETCH https://cursor.com/docs/sdk/typescript (Subagents and Restricting the toolset sections)

feature_results.rationale: The SDK documents direct function registration through local.customTools, eliminating the need for a user-operated MCP server. However, the original documentation explicitly says those functions are registered as an MCP server and called through the MCP path; disallowing mcp also removes them. The assigned definition requires a native mechanism independent of MCP, so this implementation cannot safely be marked has or partial under the supplied criteria. No separate non-MCP registration mechanism was confirmed. A complete negative protocol across all relevant source classes was not performed, so this is uncertain rather than not_found.

evidence.excerpt: Pass them on `local.customTools` and the SDK registers them as an MCP server named `custom-user-tools`. The agent discovers and calls them through the same MCP path as any other server.
Disallowing `"mcp"` also removes [custom tools](https://cursor.com/docs/sdk/typescript.md#custom-tools).

constraints.description: The discovered MCP-backed customTools API is local SDK only; cloud agents ignore it at creation and reject it on send.

Current documentation says MCP-backed custom tools skip interactive approval, including in sandboxed and auto-review runs, while deny rules and sandbox limits still apply. This does not establish an MCP-independent extension API.

queries: Find official Cursor documentation URLs for agent hooks, custom subagents and their tool restrictions, native non-MCP custom tool registration, permissions, and Plan Mode. Search only cursor.com/docs and cursor.com/changelog; identify original pages, not forum posts.
FETCH https://cursor.com/docs/sdk/typescript (offsets 0, 40000, and 60000; Custom tools and Restricting the toolset sections)

feature_results.rationale: A concrete public DPA is available and incorporated into customer contracts. Official help expressly covers Teams and Enterprise customers and excludes individual plans. Classified partial for restricted business-contract availability, rather than suggesting that a privacy policy alone qualifies or that every subscription receives a DPA.

evidence.excerpt: For Teams and Enterprise customers, the DPA and [privacy and data governance](https://cursor.com/docs/enterprise/privacy-and-data-governance.md) docs describe processor commitments and sub-processor coverage.
If you are on an individual plan, the DPA does not apply; your data handling follows the [Privacy Policy](https://cursor.com/privacy).
Customer retains ownership of all Personal Data processed under this DPA.

constraints.description: Available under Teams and Enterprise business contracts; individual plans follow the Privacy Policy instead. Enterprise plan comparison lists MSA & DPA for both Teams and Enterprise.
The DPA governs processing of Personal Data on the customer's behalf and incorporates EU/UK transfer clauses; contract signatures also serve as dated signatures for the incorporated clauses.

queries: GET https://cursor.com/docs/enterprise (DPA link and plan comparison)

feature_results.rationale: Enterprise customers can enroll individual teams in US-only residency with model inference, content processing and customer-data storage, including backups and Cloud Agents, confined to the US for in-scope features. This is a customer-requested guarantee, not just a default hosting location. Coverage is constrained by model eligibility and excludes external services and BYOK; EU + Iceland coverage is inference-only on request.

evidence.excerpt: When data residency is enabled for a team, model inference, data processing, and data storage for in-scope features stay in the selected region.
US-only data residency is available to Enterprise customers and is enabled per team.

constraints.description: Enterprise-only US residency; account-team enablement per team, with up to two weeks lead time while self-serve controls are built. Eligible model pricing has a 10% uplift.
US-only inference, processing and storage are available today. EU + Iceland inference-only coverage is available on request; broader EU/EEA and APAC support is in development.
US residency supports GPT gpt-* models, Claude 4.6+, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Composer and Grok 4.5. Unsupported models error; Auto chooses only eligible models.

Exceptions include SSO/authentication, BYOK, custom model gateways, MCPs/external integrations and @Web, repository-dependent Bugbot processing, links shared outside the team, and the issuing command for Slack/web-triggered Cloud Agents.

feature_results.rationale: Privacy Mode is an actionable settings toggle available even to free and individual users, preventing training on customer data by Cursor and model providers. Teams can enforce it centrally. It is not an unconditional no-storage guarantee: abuse investigations, explicitly approved non-ZDR models, BYOK and Cloud Agent repository storage have documented exceptions.

evidence.excerpt: Privacy Mode is available to anyone (free or Pro).
3. Toggle **Privacy Mode** on
Customer Data will not be used for training by Cursor.

constraints.description: Risk/abuse detection can trigger retention for investigation under provider retention policies. Non-ZDR models are designated or require administrator opt-in.
Some models fall outside ZDR agreements and require approval for Enterprise customers and customers with Privacy Mode enabled; opting in can apply to the whole team.
ZDR does not apply to customer-supplied API keys; the selected provider's privacy policy governs. Optional Cloud Agents store encrypted repository copies temporarily while executing.
The editor Privacy Mode guarantee is not automatically extended to the separate Grok Bot product surface and its data flows.

feature_results.rationale: Security Agents document codebase vulnerability scanning, and the changelog mentions dependency changes introducing known vulnerabilities. Neither retrieved text identifies vulnerability-database matching for project dependencies. Anybump documents remediation and reachability analysis of existing dependency tickets, which is not independently proof of SCA scanning. Cursor's first-party marketplace exposes Snyk and Sonatype-related descriptions, but the fetched content did not verify a project-dependency scan against a named vulnerability database with surfaced results. Sonatype component-data intelligence is relevant adjacent evidence, not enough to satisfy the specified has criterion. Sparse marketplace responses and incomplete integration details prevent not_found.

evidence.excerpt: **Vulnerability Scanner** scans your codebase at rest. Use it to find pre-existing vulnerabilities, long-standing issues, and problems missed during PR review.
AI-powered dependency intelligence. Check vulnerabilities, find safer versions, and make better dependency decisions using Sonatype's component data.

constraints.description: Cursor Security Agents run on the Automations platform and require Cloud Agents; this constraint describes the verified adjacent scanning workflow, not confirmation of database-backed SCA.
The documented Vulnerability Scanner does not support Bitbucket Cloud or Bitbucket Data Center repositories.

access_gaps: Marketplace pages exposed limited substantive text; Snyk/Sonatype integration details establishing project dependency scanning and database matching were not verified.
Cursor Security Agents documentation and changelog do not identify the database or confirm the precise SCA matching mechanism.
Pricing response did not expose detailed availability constraints for security integrations.

feature_results.rationale: A reviewable diff and rejection workflow are documented, but they do not establish the assigned pre-disk-write criterion: current Agent security documentation explicitly states that changes save immediately to disk, and the help page describes reviewing already-applied edits. Inline edit documentation also says Cursor applies the edit in place without documenting a pre-save, per-hunk gate. The search returned community discussions and summary claims about granular controls, which were not treated as official evidence. Research did not establish whether a separate current workflow satisfies the strict definition, so neither has nor the whole-file-only partial criterion is justified. This is not a not_found result because coverage of alternative pre-apply workflows remains incomplete.

evidence.excerpt: Agent's edits are applied as it works. Review them in the diff view and reject anything you don't want.
Agents can modify workspace files without approval, except for configuration files. Changes save immediately to disk.
Press Return. Cursor applies the edit to your selected code.

constraints.description: Agent's default review is post-write; with auto-reload, changes may execute before review.

queries: SEARCH Find official Cursor documentation on reviewing AI diffs before changes are saved to disk, inline edit Cmd K accept reject individual changes or hunks, and Agent auto-save. Look only at cursor.com or docs.cursor.com and provide original page URLs.
access_gaps: https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/inline-edit.md returned HTTP 404; its HTML counterpart was accessible but did not establish pre-save review.
No verified original official page established a separate pre-disk-write accept/reject workflow or its per-hunk granularity; alternative-workflow coverage is incomplete.

feature_results.rationale: Official technical documentation explicitly states encryption both in transit and at rest: TLS 1.2+ for Cursor services and TLS for third-party provider connections, plus AES-256 for stored data, encrypted vector storage and encrypted Cloud Agent code storage.

evidence.excerpt: Cursor encrypts data both in transit and at rest.

- TLS 1.2+ in transit
- AES-256 at rest

constraints.description: Cursor normally manages and rotates encryption keys. Standard encryption is distinct from the optional customer-managed-key feature.
Enterprise customers can request CMEK through sales for Cloud Agent data stored in Cursor infrastructure, controlling key access and rotation.

feature_results.rationale: Cursor supports SAML 2.0 organizational SSO and role-based permissions on Teams and Enterprise. Admins manage membership, roles, SSO/security, billing and analytics; Members lack most administrative privileges. Optional Enterprise SCIM automates provisioning with SSO enabled.

evidence.excerpt: Cursor supports SAML 2.0 with providers like Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and OneLogin.
Cursor teams have three roles: Members, Admins, and Unpaid Admins.
- Add/remove members, modify roles, set up SSO

constraints.description: SSO is included on Teams and Enterprise, not individual plans, according to the official plan comparison. SCIM requires Enterprise with SSO enabled.
Unpaid Admins have administrative capabilities without paid product access but require at least one paid team user.

feature_results.rationale: No qualifying full or partial offline AI operation was found. The original network-configuration documentation says Cursor needs backend services and AI providers; the API-key help says all requests pass through Cursor servers for final prompt building. Self-hosted integration documentation still requires outbound HTTPS, and CI documentation requires Internet connectivity. Cloud agents continuing after the local device disconnects and the iOS app caching conversations are not zero-network product operation. Relevant documentation, product, changelog, pricing, integration and security sources were checked, followed by targeted offline/air-gap searches. The failed .md cloud-agent URL was recovered using the extensionless official page; no material access gap remains for this decision.

constraints.description: Core agent and Tab functionality require communication with Cursor backend endpoints; network restriction is not offline operation.
Bring-your-own-key requests still route through Cursor servers for final prompt building.
Self-hosted workers require outbound HTTPS to Cursor and artifact endpoints.

feature_results.rationale: Cloud Agents clone repositories, work on separate branches and push changes as part of the product workflow. Official CLI CI documentation additionally describes agent-created branches, commits and pushes, rather than merely suggesting commands for the user to run.

evidence.excerpt: Cloud agents clone your repo from GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps Services, or Bitbucket Cloud and work on a separate branch, then push changes to your repo for handoff.
Give the agent complete control over git operations, API calls, and external interactions. Simpler setup, requires more trust.

constraints.description: The cloud repository workflow requires source control connection and read-write access to the repository and dependent repositories/submodules.
Cloud Agent runs require a paid Cursor plan.

queries: FETCH https://cursor.com/llms.txt — followed Cloud Agents and CLI navigation.
FETCH https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent.md — 404; FETCH https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent recovered full documentation.

feature_results.rationale: Print mode is explicitly non-interactive; --force allows file changes without confirmation. JSON and stream-json are documented machine-readable formats, and failure exits non-zero with stderr diagnostics. The headless example tests exit code zero for success, and a separate page documents use in GitHub Actions and other CI systems.

evidence.excerpt: Use [print mode](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/using.md#non-interactive-mode) (`-p, --print`) for non-interactive scripting and automation.

The `--force` flag allows the agent to make direct file changes without
confirmation
On failure, the process exits with a non-zero code and writes an error message to stderr. No well-formed JSON object is emitted in failure cases.
These formats include structured formats for programmatic use (`json`, `stream-json`) and a simplified text format for human-readable output (`text`).
Use Cursor CLI in GitHub Actions and other CI/CD systems to automate development tasks.

constraints.description: CI needs shell execution, API-key configuration and Internet connectivity to Cursor's API. Workflow permissions can restrict operations.
Applying file modifications in print mode requires --force (or --yolo); without it changes are proposed only.
JSON failure cases emit stderr and a non-zero exit rather than a well-formed JSON result; stream-json may terminate before the terminal result event.

queries: FETCH https://cursor.com/docs and https://cursor.com/llms.txt — followed CLI navigation.
FETCH https://cursor.com/docs/cli/overview — confirmed CI print automation.
FETCH https://cursor.com/docs/cli/headless — confirmed print, force and exit-code example.
FETCH https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/output-format — confirmed structured output and failure exit semantics.
FETCH https://cursor.com/docs/cli/github-actions — confirmed CI setup and authentication prerequisites.

feature_results.rationale: Cursor Tab generates grayed-out inline suggestions while typing, without an explicit chat request, and can modify multiple lines. The native Cursor editor workflow is confirmed for macOS, Windows, and Linux. The checked documentation does not enumerate an exhaustive supported-language matrix; no language restriction or support in every external IDE is inferred.

evidence.excerpt: Tab is Cursor's AI-powered autocomplete. It suggests code as you type, based on your recent edits, surrounding code, and linter errors.
Suggestions appear as grayed-out text ahead of your cursor.
Tab can modify multiple lines, add missing import statements, and suggest coordinated edits across related code.

constraints.description: Evidence covers Tab in the Cursor editor, with Mac and Windows/Linux shortcuts; it does not establish Tab availability in external IDE integrations.
Tab can be disabled globally, snoozed, or disabled for specific file extensions.

feature_results.rationale: The current public MSA explicitly indemnifies customers for third-party IP infringement claims involving the Service or any Suggestion, subject to exclusions. Official plan comparison links Teams and Enterprise to the MSA. Only the indemnification branch is confirmed; no built-in public-code duplication blocking setting was established, so the supplied partial criterion applies. Historical forum-based search summaries denying indemnification were not treated as evidence and are superseded by the original current legal text.

evidence.excerpt: that the Service or any Suggestion infringes or misappropriates such third party's intellectual property rights.
Anysphere shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and each of their officers, directors, employees, and agents

constraints.description: Confirmed under the MSA linked for Teams and Enterprise. No equivalent commitment is asserted for individual plans or contracts with overriding Order Form terms.

MSA exclusions include portions not created by Anysphere (including Customer Data/Third-Party Services), relevant unauthorized modifications or combinations, continued infringing use after notice, and non-compliant use.

Suggestion indemnity excludes customers who disable or interfere with content filters/safety systems, knew or should have known of likely infringement, or lack lawful rights to the Customer Data used to generate the Suggestion. A general reference to content filters does not establish a public-code matching filter.

feature_results.rationale: Cursor documents core coding functionality through Cursor Web at https://cursor.com/agents: users can start and manage Cloud Agents on any device. These agents build features, fix bugs, write tests, and open pull requests in cloud development environments rather than relying on a locally installed editor. Environment setup can also be performed through the web dashboard. This qualifies as core product access, not merely browser access to documentation or account/billing settings.

evidence.excerpt: **Cursor Web**: Start and manage agents from [cursor.com/agents](https://cursor.com/agents) on any device
You can run as many agents as you want in parallel, and they do not require your local machine to be connected to the internet.
They can build features, fix bugs, write tests, open PRs, and share a video of it working.

Let Cursor's agent set up its own environment from the [Cloud Agents dashboard](https://cursor.com/dashboard/cloud-agents#environments). The agent installs dependencies, verifies the environment, and creates its first Build.
Cloud Agents are available on all paid Cursor plans.

constraints.description: The confirmed installation-free route is Cursor Web with Cursor-hosted Cloud Agents, rather than a claim that every local desktop editor feature has browser parity.
Cloud Agents require a paid Cursor plan and are charged at the selected model's API pricing.
For existing repository work, an account admin connects GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, or Bitbucket; the user needs read-write access to the repository and dependencies.

Start from scratch is documented as an alternative without a repository or connected source control provider; it requires a paid plan and Origin setup. If an admin disables Origin, the agent starts without a repository.
Cloud Agents offer a curated selection of models, with configurable context sizes for supported models.
Web attachments have a 4 MB per-file document/image limit and a separate 15 MB video limit; ZIP document attachments are unsupported.

additional_facts.description: Automations create Cloud Agents and incur Cloud Agent usage charges. A personal or creator-owned run is billed to that person; a service-account-owned automation is billed to the team's usage pool. Automations use the model's maximum supported context window without a context-window toggle. This is usage-based automation, not an unmetered scheduler entitlement.

evidence.excerpt: Automations create cloud agents and are billed based on cloud agent usage.
Automations use each model's maximum supported context window because they run as cloud agents. There is no context-window toggle.
**Service account**: Usage is billed to the team's usage pool.

additional_facts.description: Bugbot normally reports findings with a neutral check status. Requiring the check in branch protection therefore ensures a review ran but does not, by itself, block merges on findings. Where fail-on-unresolved-issues behavior is available, it must be enabled to produce a failing status for unresolved findings. This distinction matters when treating automated review as a quality gate.

evidence.excerpt: Requiring the status alone does not block merges on findings because findings default to `neutral`.
If fail-on-unresolved-issues behavior is available for your organization, enable it to make unresolved findings produce a failing status.

Both isolate noisy intermediate work from the parent conversation and return relevant results; custom subagents are a separate user-configurable mechanism.

additional_facts.description: Privacy Mode prevents Cursor training on Customer Data and ordinarily relies on provider zero-data-retention agreements. It is not a universal no-retention promise: abuse-triggered investigations may retain data under provider policies, and non-ZDR models are designated or require administrator opt-in. With Privacy Mode off, Cursor may store and use code, prompts, editor actions, and related data to improve features and train models.

evidence.excerpt: Customer Data will not be used for training by Cursor.
Non-ZDR models will be designated as such or require an admin to opt-in to enable the model for your workspace.
we may use and store codebase data, prompts, editor actions, code snippets, and other code data and actions to improve our AI features and train our models.

additional_facts.description: Self-Hosted Machines host tool execution, not the Cursor service or inference. The full checkout, build cache, and machine-local credentials stay on the worker, but file contents needed by the agent, terminal output, diffs, screenshots, local MCP results, and routing metadata are sent to Cursor. Artifacts can be uploaded to Cursor-managed storage. Workers require outbound HTTPS; this is neither offline AI operation nor an all-data-stays-local guarantee.

evidence.excerpt: Cursor runs the agent loop, inference, and planning. Your worker performs file edits and terminal commands.
During a run, the worker sends Cursor the content the agent needs, such as file contents, terminal output, diffs, screenshots, local MCP results, and routing metadata.
The worker uploads Cloud Agent artifacts, such as screenshots, videos, and log references, to Cursor-managed storage so they can appear in pull requests and the dashboard.

additional_facts.description: Pro, Pro Plus, and Ultra have separate Cursor Models and Other Models pools that reset each monthly billing cycle. Third-party model selections draw from Other Models at the model's API rate, with additional usage available for purchase. Start, described as a plan for developers in India, covers Cursor Models but does not include Other Models. Model choice, context size, and parallel subagent work can therefore affect cost independently of subscription price.

evidence.excerpt: There are two separate usage pools, each resetting with your monthly billing cycle:
When you select a specific third-party model, usage is drawn from the **Other Models** pool at that model's API rate.
The Start plan does not include this pool.

use_cases.title: Run bounded repository maintenance from CI
use_cases.description: Invoke the headless CLI for a narrowly scoped repository task, collect structured output, and use process exit status plus independent checks to decide whether a resulting patch is acceptable. Provide authentication, Internet access, and restrictive permissions; applying edits requires the documented force option. Do not interpret JSON output as assurance of code correctness.
use_cases.rationale: The merged results confirm non-interactive print mode, JSON/stream-json output, failure exit semantics, CI integration, and independent allow/deny policies. The proposed bounded maintenance gate is inferred from those mechanisms.

use_cases.title: Generate characterization tests before refactoring
use_cases.description: Generate tests for existing or unfamiliar code using the repository's frameworks and conventions, then run them after refactoring steps to detect regressions. Automatic run-and-fix iteration requires an appropriate Auto-run configuration. Passing generated tests is useful feedback, not proof of complete behavioral equivalence.

evidence.excerpt: Before refactoring, generate tests that lock in current behavior.
Run these tests after each refactoring step to catch regressions immediately.

use_cases.title: Review pull requests continuously with Bugbot
use_cases.description: Connect a supported source-control provider, enable Bugbot on repositories, and receive review comments on updates or request a manual review where supported. Individual settings limit review to the user's own PRs; enabled team repositories can cover all contributors. Check-status configuration must be considered separately from review generation.

evidence.excerpt: Bugbot analyzes PR diffs and leaves comments with explanations and fix suggestions. It runs automatically on each PR update or manually when triggered.
Bugbot runs for all contributors to enabled repositories, regardless of team membership.

use_cases.title: Implement UI from a mockup and iterate on visual feedback
use_cases.description: Paste a screenshot, wireframe, or Figma export into a prompt, ask Agent to implement the component, and use visual feedback to refine it. Direct image input requires a vision-capable model; a Figma MCP connection is optional for richer design data rather than a prerequisite for pasted images.

evidence.excerpt: **Mockups**: Paste a wireframe or Figma export and ask the agent to build the component
**Iteration**: Take a screenshot of the current result and describe what needs to change

use_cases.title: Delegate independent maintenance tasks while retaining merge review
use_cases.description: Run separate Cloud Agents for independent maintenance changes, inspect their branches and PRs, and merge only after tests and human review. Use separate task scopes to reduce edit contention. Paid-plan eligibility, repository permissions, model costs, and team controls still apply.
use_cases.rationale: The validated features establish independently running Cloud Agents, parallel task management, branch-based work, and direct PR creation. Combining these into a maintenance queue is a workflow inference, not a new vendor guarantee.

use_cases.title: Plan and implement a test-driven feature
use_cases.description: Use Plan Mode to research the codebase and edit a stepwise implementation plan, then write and commit tests before requesting code that passes them without changing the tests. Review and verify the result before committing. The vendor documents this workflow; it does not guarantee generated code is correct.

evidence.excerpt: With Cursor's [Plan Mode](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/plan-mode.md), the agent will research your codebase, ask you clarifying questions, and produce a step-by-step plan you can edit and modify.
Tell it to make all tests pass without modifying the tests.

use_cases.title: Schedule codebase digests or trigger event-driven triage
use_cases.description: Configure an Automation with a recurring schedule or supported source-control, Slack, Linear, or webhook event, a prompt, and selected tools. Vendor examples include scheduled codebase summaries and Slack bug triage. Code-changing automations need repository selection; Cloud Agent usage is billed and scheduled execution may be delayed.

evidence.excerpt: Cursor Automations run [cloud agents](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent.md) in the background, either on a schedule or in response to events from GitHub, GitLab, Slack, webhooks, Linear, and more.
Scheduled triggers may run with a delay but will not start before the indicated time.

use_cases.title: Standardize agent work across a team
use_cases.description: Combine enforced team guidance, version-controlled project rules, lifecycle checks, and appropriate administrator controls to make repository work more consistent. Test the policies and review outcomes; not all hook failures block actions, and instruction precedence is not a substitute for an execution security boundary.
use_cases.rationale: The validated hierarchy, persistent rule files, hooks, and organizational access controls support this combined workflow. It remains an inference, with Teams/Enterprise and Enterprise-only distribution constraints retained rather than assuming all controls exist on every plan.

release_history.summary: Announced beta Projects, rolling out to users, with a cloud coordinator that plans and delegates work rather than writing code itself. Shared context files synchronize across project agents, and subscriptions support schedules or external signals. This records the dated beta announcement, not a claim of generally available deployment or unlimited effective capacity.

evidence.excerpt: Cursor Projects
Projects are available in beta and rolling out to all users starting today.
Each Project maintains a set of files that sync across every cloud and local machine its agents use.

release_history.summary: Added viewing and replying to local computer agents from the Cursor iOS app. Pairing requires approval in the desktop app, and the computer must remain on and online. Remote control is enabled by default except for Enterprise organizations, whose administrators can enable it. It does not require Cloud Agents.

evidence.excerpt: Remote control for local agents
You can now see and reply to the local agents running on your computer from the Cursor iOS app.
Your computer needs to stay on and online for remote control to work.

release_history.summary: Launched Teams/Enterprise bots for per-environment deployment health monitoring and security review of pull requests. Rollouts connects source control, deployment events, and telemetry; it can propose a revert PR or hand a regression to an agent but does not merge or roll back autonomously. Security Review reports exploitable bugs with severity, attack path, and a proposed fix; draft PRs are skipped.

evidence.excerpt: Rollouts and Security Review
Both are available today on Teams and Enterprise plans.
Rollouts does not merge or roll back on its own today.
Each finding carries a severity, the attack path, and a proposed fix.

release_history.summary: Announced self-hosted tool execution with personal machines, dynamically scheduled team worker pools, partner sandbox integrations, and Linux/Mac computer use. The announcement concerns the tool-execution component; current technical documentation retains Cursor-hosted inference and the agent loop, so this is not an on-premises release of the whole service.

self-hosted machines
